title: Canonical ANet membership convergence keeps provenance occurrences and ExactSequence multiplicity distinct
semanticClaim: Deriving the same canonical Link more than once yields one semantic ANet membership.
The order in which independent Link contributions arrive is nonsemantic at the ANet membership level.
Distinct derivation/provenance events may remain distinct evidence occurrences even when they project to the same semantic Link membership.
ANet membership idempotence does not collapse repeated positions in ExactSequence: [X,X] remains distinct from [X].
explicitPremises: Semantic ANet state is interpreted extensionally as Link membership.
Contribution convergence is stated only at the semantic membership projection.
Provenance/evidence is carried separately from semantic membership.
ExactSequence is a recursive positional Link carrier and preserves order and multiplicity.
exclusions: No proof is claimed that physical storage has only one record for a canonical Link.
No runtime deduplication opcode or separate semantic command is introduced.
No provenance event is erased merely because another event derives the same Link.
ExactSequence is not treated as ordinary extensional ANet membership.
This does not close generation isolation or scheduler/partition refinement; those are GPR-03 and GPR-04.
